Billerud: a real recovery in the price-cost spread that the share price already reflects, with the disputed second step of earnings growth tested between July and October 2027

24 November 2026. Share price SEK 89.15 (19 November 2026); market value about SEK 22bn; enterprise value about SEK 28bn. All money is in Swedish kronor (SEK). Next results: 2 February 2027. Bases, sources and model notes are in the end notes.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

Billerud's recovery is real, and most of it has already happened and been paid for. Billerud's EBITDA in the second half of 2026 is running at about SEK 4.4bn a year, almost double the first-half rate. Our 2027 EBITDA forecast is that run-rate plus 3%; consensus needs the run-rate plus 12%. The shares have risen 43% in six months and are priced on the consensus version of 2027.
The calendar is the most useful thing to understand about this case. The next two reports (2 February and late April 2027) should look strong against a very weak first half of 2026, but they test only the part of the forecast that nobody disputes. The disputed part, a further SEK 0.5bn of EBITDA, is tested between July and October 2027, after the storm-salvage wood supply has gone and about 1.45Mt of new UK recycled containerboard capacity is running. Good news in February is therefore not evidence that consensus is right.

The case in seven points:

  1. Billerud's earnings are driven by the price-cost spread, not by demand. Four things set Billerud's profit: the selling prices of its virgin-fibre grades, the cost of Nordic wood (which it buys almost entirely from others), the krona and self-help. Each of the four moves EBITDA by more than any plausible change in volume. Demand is bottoming, not recovering.
  2. Self-help is the dependable part of the 2027 forecast. About SEK 0.45bn of the 2027 EBITDA increase comes from savings, maintenance and efficiency, which management controls and has a record of delivering. In total, about SEK 3.8bn to 3.9bn of the SEK 4.5bn 2027 EBITDA forecast rests on actions already taken or prices already set.
  3. The gap between our forecast and consensus is one point of price. Our 2027 EBITDA is 9% below consensus and our 2027 EPS is 22% below. One extra point of group selling price, held for the whole year, closes the entire gap, which shows how thin the margin for error is in both directions.
  4. The range of 2027 outcomes is wide and leans down. Four outcomes in five for 2027 EBITDA should fall between SEK 3.8bn and SEK 5.2bn (EPS SEK 2.2 to 6.6). I put the chance of 2027 EBITDA reaching consensus at about one in four.
  5. Estimate upgrades have driven the shares, and the easy upgrades are done. Billerud is the only stock in its sector with strongly rising estimates. Those upgrades are operating leverage on small changes in EBITDA, and the A rating for sell-side momentum that they earned will fade as they leave the three-month window in February.
  6. The return on our forecasts is modest. At the guideline fair multiple of 15.5x, the model gives a total shareholder return of +9% to 31 March 2028 and +23% to 30 September 2029, about 6.5% to 7.5% a year. Earnings growth and dividends supply all of that return; the change in multiple subtracts about 14%.
  7. Three developments would turn Billerud into the positively skewed situation Richard looks for. They are shown in the three green cards below.

Route to a positive skew 1: a closure

A capacity closure in European board, by Billerud or by a peer, would add EBITDA that no forecast contains.

Route to a positive skew 2: cheap wood and firm board prices

Wood costs staying at their late-2026 low through 2027, together with a firm liquid packaging board price, would deliver most of consensus.

Route to a positive skew 3: a lower entry price

Near book-value support (SEK 58 to 67 a share), the same forecasts would sit above what the share price reflects.

The five judgements that move the shares most

One conversion from EBITDA to share value runs through all five judgements, and the chain below shows it. Depreciation (about SEK 2.87bn) and interest (about SEK 0.2bn) do not move with these drivers, which is why small changes in EBITDA become large changes in EPS.

The arithmetic behind each judgement, step by step:

  • Wood. A 10% move in the Nordic pulpwood price is worth about SEK 0.9bn of EBITDA, so Billerud's wood bill is about SEK 9bn. A five-point error is therefore SEK 450m of EBITDA; after tax (× 0.78) it is SEK 351m; divided by 248.7m shares it is SEK 1.41, or 28% of FY2028 EPS. In the scarce grades, part of a rise in wood costs is recovered in price with a lag, and the forecast already assumes about SEK 0.15bn of that recovery.
  • Price. One point of group selling price is about SEK 0.4bn of revenue, and almost all of it reaches EBITDA. After tax it is SEK 312m, or SEK 1.25 a share, which is 28% of FY2027 EPS. Within this sensitivity sits the January 2027 liquid packaging board price round: ±3% on that grade's price is ±SEK 0.25bn of EBITDA, or ±SEK 0.78 of EPS, and the outcome becomes known on 2 February.
  • Krona. A 10% stronger krona removes about SEK 640m of EBITDA before hedges, or SEK 64m for each point. If EUR/SEK reaches 10.40 by the end of 2027, as Morgan Stanley expects, the krona would be about four points stronger than the forecast carries for 2028: SEK 256m of EBITDA, SEK 200m after tax and SEK 0.80 a share. Revenue would fall by about 4% × 82% foreign-currency share × SEK 41.9bn, or SEK 1.4bn.
  • North America. One and a half points of margin on about SEK 12.1bn of Region North America revenue is SEK 180m of EBITDA; after tax it is SEK 141m, or SEK 0.57 a share, which is 13% of FY2027 EPS.
  • Capacity. The closure of a 200kt to 300kt high-cost unit, or a peer's closure that lifts industry operating rates, could add SEK 0.2bn to 0.4bn of EBITDA within 12 to 18 months: SEK 0.63 to 1.25 a share. The opposite error is a board price attack by a competitor trying to fill a machine, which I put at 15% to 20% likely: a 5% to 10% fall in the liquid packaging board price is SEK 0.4bn to 0.8bn of EBITDA, or SEK 1.25 to 2.5 a share.
Judgements 1 to 3 (wood, price and the krona) are correlated in the bad case. If wood costs rise, prices slip and the krona strengthens together (about one chance in six to eight), 2027 EBITDA is SEK 3.5bn to 3.9bn and 2027 EPS is SEK 1.3 to 2.5.

Grades: A 90 to 100, B 75 to 89, C 50 to 74, D 25 to 49, F 1 to 24. Scores set by the Rater.

#1 Tailwinds in the operating environment, and the absence of headwinds

The operating environment is a real tailwind for about two more quarters. The tailwind works through the price-cost spread, not through demand, and the forces that will offset it have known dates.

The evidence.

Three forces help now

  • Virgin-fibre (fresh-fibre) paper is scarce. No new virgin-fibre machine is planned in Europe; North American producers closed about 10% of their capacity between early 2025 and mid-2026; and US exports to Europe fell by a third. Unbleached kraftliner prices are up EUR 200 a tonne from their early-2026 low, sack paper prices are up EUR 50 a tonne, and semichemical fluting is sold out.
  • Swedish wood became cheaper. Storm Johannes felled about 10 million cubic metres of timber, and Swedish pulpwood prices dropped 15% to 20% from their third-quarter 2025 highs. Cheaper wood reaches Billerud's accounts three to six months after purchase, so the benefit sits in the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027.
  • Billerud makes its own energy. Billerud's European mills are about 98% fossil-free. The autumn gas price spike (EUR 78 to 100 per MWh) raises recycled-fibre rivals' costs by about EUR 15 a tonne for each EUR 10 per MWh, and leaves Billerud's costs unaffected.

Three forces hurt, and they are not going away

  • Demand reflects restocking and price rises, not end use. Volumes rose in 2026 because customers stopped destocking and bought ahead of price rises. European consumer confidence is weak, weak construction holds sack paper volumes 11% below their 2021 level, and brokers model only about 1% a year of growth in European board demand.
  • Cartonboard is oversupplied. Stora Enso's 750kt Oulu line reaches full output by the end of 2027, and Chinese exports of virgin-fibre board have doubled.
  • Graphic paper, about 22% of sales, shrinks about 5% a year. Graphic paper is the cash base of Billerud's North American business.

Two further headwinds have fixed dates: the storm-salvage wood supply ends over the winter, and about 1.45Mt of UK recycled containerboard capacity starts from March 2027.

The inference. The tailwinds explain why 2026 is the trough and why the first half of 2027 is strong, and they are mostly in the run-rate already. Management's own wording on wood supports this reading. Management guides the 2027 average wood cost as "stable" against the 2026 average; because the 2026 average includes expensive first-half wood, a stable annual average implies wood costs rising during 2027.

Where I differ from the market. The prevailing narrative calls Billerud "the purest way to own" scarce fresh fibre and cheaper Swedish wood. I agree with that description and with the outlook for the next two quarters. I differ on duration: consensus numbers carry the tailwinds through all of 2027 and add to them.

One point is under-discussed, and it cuts both ways. The premium of virgin-fibre over recycled containerboard prices (EUR 230 a tonne, against a ten-year average of EUR 80) can narrow because recycled prices rise with gas costs, not only because virgin prices fall. What matters to Billerud is the kraftliner price itself, not the premium. While gas prices stay high, the argument that the virgin premium "must collapse" is weaker than it looks.

The strongest counter-case. DNB Carnegie expects Scandinavian wood prices to keep falling through 2027, and the sector note judges that virgin-fibre mills can keep raising prices for 12 to 24 months. If both views hold, the tailwind lasts all of 2027 and consensus is right.

What would change my view. Three public, monthly signals: spring 2027 forest-owner price lists that are flat or lower; the kraftliner index holding after the new King's Lynn mill in the UK starts; and gas staying above about EUR 60 per MWh.

Conclusion: the tailwinds are strong but narrow and already in the run-rate, and dated headwinds follow from mid-2027, so this attribute is met for the next two quarters and not beyond.

Score: 54, set by the Rater. Three real external forces (scarce virgin fibre with kraftliner up EUR 200/t, Swedish wood down 15-20% after the storm, self-generated energy against a gas spike) lift the price-cost spread through about mid-2027. Against them sit dated direct threats (salvage wood ending, 1.45Mt of UK recycled capacity from March 2027, oversupplied cartonboard) and structural drags (graphic paper, 22% of sales, shrinking 5% a year; demand only refill at about 1% growth), so over two to three years the net is a small, front-loaded positive, coherent with the External change forces group at 54, above Kerry's neutral environment and below OEM International's modestly positive one.

#2 Internally driven corporate change, and the absence of problems

Self-help is the best-evidenced part of the case. Billerud's self-help is deep, narrow and nearly used up, and the one internal lever that would change mid-term earnings, a European capacity closure, has not been pulled.

The evidence.

Delivered

  • Cost. The SEK 800m savings programme delivers SEK 550m in 2026 and the rest in 2027; all 650 planned position reductions were completed by April 2026. Its SEK 1.5bn predecessor programme finished a year early.
  • Capital discipline. Billerud cancelled the SEK 7bn Escanaba mill conversion in 2024 and replaced it with a SEK 1.3bn incremental programme (Evolution). Capex guidance has been cut twice, and Billerud exited a joint venture that would have needed more capital.
  • People. Both regional presidents were replaced with operators from UPM, International Paper and Sonoco.
  • North American packaging. Quarterly volumes from the packaging conversion have risen from 3kt to 11kt in five quarters (chart below). Continuing at the same pace gives about 80kt in 2027, which is all the forecast needs.

Against this

  • Returns to shareholders are falling. The 2025 dividend was cut to SEK 2.00, against expectations of SEK 3.30 to 3.50, and Billerud bought back no shares even with the shares at 0.55x book value.
  • The next capital call is defensive. The Gävle recovery boiler (above SEK 3bn, with a decision due in 2027) is replacement spending that earns roughly the cost of capital. I think a final cost of SEK 3.5bn or more is as likely as not.
  • North American execution is patchy. Both North American shutdowns in 2026 overran, and Region North America missed consensus by 13% in the third quarter.
  • Management turnover continues below the top two executives. The executive who runs strategic projects, the function that would carry out a closure or an acquisition, leaves at the end of 2026.

The inference.

Cost programmes at Billerud are a shield, not an engine. About SEK 2.3bn of savings since 2023 left EBITDA roughly where it started, because higher wood costs, lost carbon-allowance income and lower prices absorbed the savings. No savings programme is named for the years after 2027, so further margin gains must come from the market, the North American ramp-up or a closure.

Billerud's cost programmes also carry a signal. Billerud launched them in 2023 and in September 2025, both times as the spread deteriorated. A new cost programme in late 2027 would therefore be a warning as much as good news.

Where I differ from the market. The market credits the self-help, and I agree. Jefferies wants "strategic actions" before turning positive, and I agree with that too. My addition is the balance sheet. Billerud has the strongest balance sheet among the non-integrated European producers at a time when competitors are under strain (Metsä Board; Mayr-Melnhof, with its impairments; insolvencies among smaller mills). That balance sheet gives Billerud real options: to close capacity, to swap assets or to buy. Management's record says it uses the balance sheet for resilience, not for returns, so I do not count on these options. They are, however, the one positive lever within the company's control that is in neither the share price nor any forecast.

The strongest counter-case. An operating team hired from UPM, a chief executive who says closures and deals are "on the table", and a board that has shown it will walk away from poor returns could act sooner than I assume.

What would change my view. A closure announcement; any discussion of share buybacks; or approval of Gävle as the cheaper "intermediate solution".

Conclusion: the corporate change forces are strong and proven on cost and capital discipline, but narrow, largely banked by 2027 and silent on footprint and shareholder returns, so the attribute is met in part.

Score: 58, set by the Rater. Self-help is proven and material for the size of today's earnings: the SEK 800m programme (SEK 550m in 2026, the rest in 2027, its predecessor closed a year early), the Escanaba cancellation, two capex cuts and new operator regional presidents supply about SEK 0.45bn of the 2027 increase, and the North American packaging ramp is on track. But it is repair of a cyclical business, not an engine (SEK 2.3bn of savings since 2023 left EBITDA where it started), and it is netted by a dividend cut, no buyback at 0.55x book, a defensive Gävle boiler call of SEK 3bn or more, overrunning North American shutdowns and the strategic-projects head leaving, so it sits just above Shell's incremental self-help and below Odfjell Drilling, in line with the group's 57.

#3 Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile and management

Billerud holds good positions in the wrong part of the value chain. Its niches are real, its returns are below the cost of capital, and its management is competent but defensive.

The evidence.

  • Positions. Billerud is global number two in liquid packaging board (the board inside milk and juice cartons, about 22% of sales); number two in European sack paper and in semichemical fluting; and number two in North American coated freesheet, with about 41% of that market. A carton maker takes two to four years to qualify a new board supplier.
  • The structural weakness. Billerud owns almost no forest (under 5% self-sufficiency in wood) and is the largest buyer of Nordic pulpwood. More than 80% of its revenue is in foreign currency, while more than half of its costs are in kronor. Billerud sits in the two least profitable stages of its value chain; forest owners and carton converters earn the stable margins.
  • Returns. Return on capital employed was 4.0% in 2025, against 12.8% at forest-owning Holmen, and the forecast reaches only about 5% in 2027 and 7% in 2030. Billerud's own 11% target needs about SEK 3.7bn of operating profit, against SEK 1.6bn forecast for 2027.
  • North America is the better business. Wood in North America costs 30% to 40% less than in Sweden, the market is consolidated and protected by tariffs, and Region North America earned about half of 2025 EBITDA on a third of sales.
  • Management. Billerud has a finance-led operating team and clean governance. Management delivers what it controls and explains near-term mechanics unusually well. Its ambition is defensive: its target of SEK 6bn of EBITDA "over a cycle" is not reached in our forecast in any year to 2030, and it has not out-executed peers in tough markets.
The inference: in its European virgin-fibre grades, Billerud is itself the marginal-cost producer. The consequence is easy to miss: prices in those grades tend to follow Billerud's own wood cost, with a lag. Margin gains are therefore real while wood costs fall, and they are given back as wood costs rise. Over a full cycle, this is why Billerud's niches protect volume better than they protect margin.

Where I differ from the market. The market values Billerud at about 6x EBITDA, against 16x for forest-owning SCA, and at about 0.8x book value. That discount is deserved, and I agree with it. I see slightly more value than the market in two places: the North American wood-cost and tariff position, which is durable and carries the group through bad European years; and the balance sheet. Neither changes my conclusion that Billerud is a medium-quality cyclical.

The strongest counter-case. The wood shock of 2022 to 2025 may have been a one-off supply event, caused by the loss of Russian wood imports. If Nordic wood prices have now reset lower for several years, Billerud's niches would show their true earning power, and the SEK 6bn EBITDA target would be within reach.

What would change my view. Returns above 8% held through a year of rising wood costs; a long-term wood supply arrangement at scale; or a closure that removes the highest-cost European tonnes.

Conclusion: industry positions are good and the balance sheet is sound, but the business model has no forest and little pricing power outside scarce grades, and returns sit below the cost of capital, so this attribute is not met.

Score: 35, set by the Rater. The niches are real (global number two in liquid packaging board with two-to-four-year qualification, number two in European sack paper and fluting, a tariff-protected, low-wood-cost North American business), but the group owns under 5% of its wood, is the marginal-cost producer in its European grades so price follows its own wood cost, has more than half its costs in kronor against 80% foreign revenue, and sits in the two least profitable stages of the chain; management is competent and disciplined but defensive. The financial profile confirms it rather than misleading: return on invested capital (ROIC) 2.1% (18th percentile), operating margin 2.6% (8th), EPS down 48% a year over three years (4th), with returns forecast at only 5-7% to 2030, below the cost of capital, and only the 1.6x leverage keeps it off the floor; this matches the groups (45, 36, 26, 52) and places it just below CVS Group and above Solid State.

#4 Guidance, the management of expectations and the record of delivery

Billerud gives no annual earnings guidance, so the usual chain from raised guidance to raised estimates does not exist here. Management is conservative on what it controls, silent on what it does not control, and does nothing to manage consensus down.

The evidence.

What management guides, and has delivered

Next-quarter building blocks in kronor and percent (maintenance by mill, input costs, price by region, the direction of wood costs), plus savings, capex and hedges. Billerud has met or beaten these blocks, and it raised the 2026 savings target from SEK 500m to SEK 550m.

What management does not guide

Annual revenue, annual EBITDA, or any bridge to the SEK 6bn EBITDA target. That target is about 25% above the five-year average, under worse wood and carbon conditions than the period it is measured against. The SEK 6bn target is the opposite of conservative.
  • Consensus sits above management's guided building blocks. Management's blocks for 2027 (savings, stable wood costs, positive pricing into the first half) support perhaps SEK 0.4bn to 0.8bn of EBITDA increase. Consensus has about SEK 1.5bn. Nothing management has said endorses the difference, and nothing it has said pushes back on it.
  • The record against estimates is volatile and lopsided. EBITDA misses of 24% to 28% (Q2 2025 and Q1 2026) compare with beats of 3% to 16%. Misses cluster in the fourth and first quarters, and the last two quarters were beats. In the last comparable early recovery (late 2023 to 2024), a run of beats was followed by misses once wood costs rose.
  • Targets and dividends have been cut, not raised. The margin target was cut from 17% to 15% in December 2024.

The inference. Billerud's reputation for "conservative guidance" is true only of the controllable items, where over-delivery might be worth SEK 50m to 100m of EBITDA. That amount is small beside the SEK 0.4bn value of one point of price. The quarterly outlooks are directionally reliable, which helps investors track the case but does not create upgrades.

Where I differ from the market: the A rating for sell-side momentum does not mean Billerud is beating and raising. The upgrades came from brokers catching up with a recovery in costs and wood, not from management lifting anything. The centre of expectations is also higher than it looks. FactSet's mean cannot be reproduced from the five brokers it names, so unseen contributors must sit above SEK 5bn; the 2027 EBITDA figure that results will actually be judged against is SEK 4.8bn to 5.0bn.

The strongest counter-case. A chief executive who does not talk up the market, guides in checkable blocks and has just raised a savings target is exactly the kind who under-promises. Two beats in a row may be the start of a longer run.

What would change my view. Management steering 2027 expectations explicitly; a capital markets day that re-bases targets to levels the forecast can reach; or a third and fourth beat that come from price and volume, not cost.

Conclusion: guidance is specific and dependable for a quarter ahead but absent for the year, consensus is not being kept conservative, and the delivery record has larger misses than beats, so this attribute is largely not met.

Score: 40, set by the Rater. There is no annual guidance (neutral in itself), and the quarterly building blocks, savings, capex and hedges are met or beaten, with the 2026 savings target raised from SEK 500m to SEK 550m. But the record against consensus is lopsided (EBITDA misses of 24-28% in Q2 2025 and Q1 2026 against beats of 3-16%, only the last two quarters beaten), the margin target was cut from 17% to 15%, the dividend was cut well below expectations, the SEK 6bn target is unreached in any forecast year, and management does nothing to pull a consensus that sits about SEK 0.7-1.1bn above its guided blocks back down; the sell-side upgrades are brokers catching up, not management raising, so it sits below Instalco and just above Hexatronic, coherent with the Guidance (45) and Sell-side (40) groups.

#5 Pricing power, operating and financial leverage, cost scope and feedback loops

Billerud's operating leverage is very high, and it cuts both ways. A small rise in revenue produces outsized profit growth, a small adverse move in price or wood cost produces an outsized fall, and the business lacks the pricing power to choose which.

The evidence.

  • Operating leverage. In 2027 EBITDA rises by about a third and EPS almost fourfold on revenue growth of under 3%. The incremental margin is about 100%, because the drivers of the increase (savings, maintenance, wood and price) change profit without changing volume. Depreciation is fixed at about 7% of sales, so operating profit is only about 4% of sales, and every krona of change in EBITDA falls straight to operating profit.
  • Pricing power. Pricing power is real only in the scarce grades (about 40% of sales) and behind US tariffs (about 22%). Across the group, selling prices were still below a year earlier in the second and third quarters of 2026. The decisive test came between 2021 and 2025: wood costs doubled and the industry could not pass the increase on. Management itself calls today's price rises "cost-driven".
  • Liquid packaging board pricing moves faster than it looks. All of Billerud's liquid packaging board volume is now on one-year price terms: the volume is sticky, but the price is not. That makes earnings less stable from year to year than Stora Enso's, but more stable within a year, because the price is fixed each January.
  • Financial leverage is small. Interest is about 4% to 5% of EBITDA, and net debt falls to about 1.2x EBITDA by the end of 2027. The low debt protects the downside and adds nothing to the upside.
  • Cost scope. The easy fixed costs are already out. The remaining scope is in procurement, efficiency and capacity.
  • Feedback loops. Balancing loops dominate. Cheaper wood is given back in price in oversupplied grades; a wide virgin-fibre premium attracts recycled supply; storm wood felled today means less felling later; and recovering exporters strengthen the krona. The reinforcing loops (tariffs speeding up US customer qualification; competitor distress forcing closures) are slower or have no date.

The inference. Revenue is a poor indicator to monitor for Billerud. In each of the last three years, the change in EBITDA was between 3 and 20 times the change in revenue. The bad years share one structure: wood costs and selling prices decouple for supply reasons, and weak demand does not hedge that decoupling. The main adverse case for late 2027 has the same structure.

Where I differ from the market: the upgrades are gearing on a small change, not a broadening recovery. The market sees leverage working upward, with 2027 consensus EPS up 20% in three months. Over the same three months, consensus EBITDA is up only 6% and consensus sales only 1%. The same gearing would work in reverse.

The strongest counter-case. With leverage this high, the bull case needs very little: one point of price. Two helpful interactions also exist. If wood costs rise, customers lose their argument for price cuts, so errors in wood and price do not fully stack. And a gas price shock supports the price of every virgin-fibre grade.

What would change my view. A price rise that sticks after its cost justification has reversed. Such a rise would be the test of pricing power, and Billerud has not yet passed it.

Conclusion: operating leverage is exceptional and financial risk is low, but without durable pricing power the leverage is symmetric, so this attribute is met in mechanism and not in quality.

Score: 50, set by the Rater. Operating leverage is very high in structure: fixed depreciation of about 7% of sales leaves operating profit at about 4%, the incremental margin on price and wood is about 100%, and mill curtailments make volume losses worse than proportional, so 2027 EPS roughly quadruples on under 3% revenue growth. But pricing power is real only in scarce grades and behind US tariffs (about 60% of sales at best), the 2021-25 wood doubling could not be passed on, financial leverage is small (interest 4-5% of EBITDA), the easy fixed costs are already out, and balancing loops dominate, so the gearing is to a spread the company does not set and is symmetric; that is the levels' asymmetric-leverage-without-pricing-power case at about 50, above Maersk's pure price gearing and level with BP, and coherent with the Economic strength (26) and Financial forecasts (40) groups only once the structure, not today's margin, is judged.

#6 Forecast financials

The forecast is a front-loaded recovery to about SEK 4.5bn of EBITDA in 2027, a plateau in 2028 and a slow drift up to a neutral-cycle SEK 5.0bn to 5.3bn. EPS grows at double-digit rates from a trough, but margins only return to the long-run average and returns stay below the cost of capital.

FY2025 is on the brokers' basis. Notes on the FY2026 tax rate and on the model's Q4 2026 figure are in the end notes.

What builds 2027: three independent routes reach the same EBITDA within SEK 0.15bn. The model's bridge from SEK 3,378m in 2026 (chart below) reaches about SEK 4,500m, and price is its largest single block. The later research amends six of the bridge items (carbon to nil, a flat liquid packaging board price round, a smaller krona cost, and less credit for efficiency and for the non-repeat of the North American overruns); the amendments offset each other and give SEK 4,450m. A separate rebuild from the second-half 2026 run-rate gives about SEK 4.6bn. Because three routes agree this closely, I leave the model's inputs unchanged.

The shape of 2027 matters more than its level. Our quarterly EBITDA runs at about SEK 1.16bn, 1.16bn, 1.09bn, 1.12bn and 1.13bn from Q4 2026 to Q4 2027. Against a year earlier, that is growth of about +122% and +64% in the first two quarters of 2027, then +8% and -2%. All of 2027's growth therefore comes from two comparisons with an abnormally weak first half of 2026, and a flat fourth quarter of 2027 is the expected path, not a miss.

Against the past.

  • Growth. EPS compounds at about 14% a year from 2027 to 2030, but this growth is recovery, not compounding: EPS has swung between about SEK 2 and SEK 20 since 2019. Revenue grows 2.5% a year, mostly from price.
  • Margins. The 12.0% EBITDA margin reached in 2030 equals the seven-year average. The forecast leaves no scope for margins above the past, because about SEK 0.5bn a year of carbon-allowance income has gone for good and wood is structurally dearer.
  • Cash. Free cash flow turns consistently positive after three years that averaged about SEK -0.6bn, but the Gävle boiler absorbs it from 2028. Cash after dividends is roughly nil, and leverage drifts to about 1.0x to 1.2x EBITDA.

Where I differ from the market. Consensus has EBITDA margins of 11.8% in 2027 and 12.3% in 2028, and free cash flow 50% to 70% higher than ours. Consensus capex for 2028 leaves almost no room for Gävle. I agree with consensus on the direction and on the first half of 2027; I disagree on the second step and on cash.

The strongest counter-case. Three developments together would deliver consensus: wood flat at its late-2026 level through 2027 (about +SEK 0.2bn to 0.3bn of EBITDA against our path), a liquid packaging board price up 2% to 3% (about +SEK 0.2bn) and EUR/SEK at 11 (about +SEK 0.1bn). Each is plausible alone, but consensus needs most of them at once.

What would change my view. The February report. Group EBITDA below about SEK 1.05bn, or a Region Europe margin below 12%, would mean a building block of the forecast has failed; a rise in the liquid packaging board price would add to our 2027 forecast.

Conclusion: the forecast offers double-digit EPS growth from a trough but not higher margins or returns than the past, and it sits 9% (EBITDA) and 22% (EPS) below consensus, so the attribute is met on growth and not on quality.

Score: 64, set by the Rater. Above 35% gives C, and the cut-off's caution fits exactly: almost all of it is the 2027 recovery from a trough year (EPS up about 3.7 times on 2.8% revenue growth), and the 14% a year from 2027 to 2030 that follows would only reach B. I place it in the upper middle of C because the growth is organic and real (about SEK 3.8-3.9bn of the SEK 4.5bn 2027 EBITDA rests on actions taken or prices set), but held down because margins only return to the seven-year average of 12% by 2030, free cash flow after dividends is about nil, and the path sits 22% below consensus EPS.

#7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

The scope for upgrades is small, short-lived and mostly at the bottom of the broker range. Over twelve months, estimate cuts are more likely than rises, but the cuts come late.

Guidance. There is no annual guidance to raise. The one guided item likely to disappoint consensus is the 2026 dividend: we forecast SEK 1.50 against consensus of SEK 2.00, and I put about 65% on a figure below SEK 2.00. Reported 2026 profit is only about SEK 0.9 a share, and the Gävle decision is pending.

Estimates. The chart below shows my view of how 2027 consensus EBITDA will move at each report.

Over the whole twelve months, the odds lean to a cut:

60%2027 consensus EBITDA ends lower than today
20%2027 consensus EBITDA ends within 2% of today
20%2027 consensus EBITDA ends higher than today
65%The 2026 dividend comes in below the SEK 2.00 consensus

A 9% cut to 2027 EBITDA would be a 22% cut to EPS. Cash-flow estimates face a dated cut of their own: when Gävle is approved, capex estimates should rise by SEK 0.4bn to 1.2bn a year, and hopes for dividends and buybacks should fall.

Narrative. Today's story is "recovery". Unless capacity closes, I expect the story to become "how much of the recovery sticks" during 2027, and the market usually prices that story on lower multiples.

Three positive surprises are in neither the share price nor the numbers. They are a closure or consolidation step; a flat-to-higher liquid packaging board price, helped by the long outage at Nippon's Dynawave mill (about 8% of world supply); and a tight US board market. On the board price, I am slightly more positive than Jefferies.

Where I differ from the market. Nothing important here is unknown. The favourable facts are in both the share price and consensus. The unfavourable facts are stated plainly by the two Hold-rated brokers but are absent from the consensus numbers. Our base case is close to Jefferies' published view: a minority view, not a new one. Three points are little discussed anywhere:

  • The currency hedges are a rolling 15-month programme, not a cliff, so the krona's effect is smoothed into 2028. The research holds two readings of the hedge percentages, and the point holds on either reading.
  • Consensus contains almost no Gävle spending.
  • The estimate upgrades are operating leverage on small EBITDA changes.

The strongest counter-case. The brokers above SEK 5bn may simply be right about wood and price, in which case 2027 brings a second year of upgrades.

What would change my view. A liquid packaging board price rise announced on 2 February; flat wood price lists in the spring; or a closure announcement.

Conclusion: the probability of upgrades is not skewed to the positive beyond the next report or two, and over twelve months it is skewed to cuts, so this attribute is not met.

Score: 25, set by the Rater. There is no annual guidance line to raise and the one guided cash item, the dividend, is about 65% likely to come in below the SEK 2.00 consensus, with Gävle capex absent from consensus; on 2027 consensus EBITDA the memo puts about 60% on a cut over twelve months against 20% on a rise, and a 9% EBITDA gap is a 22% EPS gap against revenue growth of under 3%, a strongly negative ratio even though the next one or two reports may still lift the low-end brokers. The narrative is likely to move from 'recovery' to 'how much sticks'; with cuts more likely than raises but arriving late, it sits between Indutrade (downgrades as likely as upgrades) and Xvivo (downgrades clearly likelier), coherent with the fourth-set group at 30.

#8 Current momentum: guidance, estimates, narrative, share price and peers

Billerud's momentum is strong, late and specific to this one stock; no sector move supports it.

The evidence (dashboard, 19 November 2026).

Sell-side momentumATechnical momentumDValuationDThematic fitD
  • Sell-side momentum: A. 2027 consensus EPS is up 10%, 20% and 25% over one, three and six months, and target prices are up 18% over six months. But the share of Buy ratings fell 10 points over three months to 70%, after Jefferies and DNB Carnegie moved to Hold on valuation in late September and early October.
  • Technical momentum: D. The share price is 21% above its 200-day moving average and relative strength is at the 81st percentile, but the 200-day average has risen in only one of the last twelve months. The shares are up 43% in six months but only 5% in twelve.
  • Valuation: D; thematic fit: D.
  • Guidance momentum is limited to the raised 2026 savings figure.
  • Peers. Every other stock in the sector rates C to F on earnings momentum, except SIG at B. The peer basket fell about 8% in the six months in which Billerud rose 39%. Holmen missed third-quarter consensus by 14%, Mondi also missed, SCA was downgraded to Hold, and Mayr-Melnhof warned on energy costs on 19 November.

The inference. Day to day, a little under half of Billerud's share-price movement is shared with the sector, and its beta is about 1.1. Over the last six months, however, almost none of its return came from the sector. The re-rating rests on one company-specific fact: Billerud is the only stock in its sector with strongly rising estimates. That fact leaves the shares fully exposed to delivery, in both directions. If the upgrades stop, the natural comparison becomes peers trading at the low end of their valuation ranges on falling estimates.

The A rating for sell-side momentum should fade without any estimate cut. The upgrades that produced the A rating were made between late October and early November 2026, and by early February 2027 they leave the three-month measurement window. To keep the rating, brokers would have to raise 2027 EPS by a similar amount again, which would take it above every named broker's forecast.

Where I differ from the market. The market reads Billerud's momentum as broad and early; I read it as narrow and about six months old. Precedent in this sector says that phases of rising estimates last 12 to 18 months and are usually ended by wood costs or new capacity. The current phase began around mid-2026, so twelve to eighteen months on is mid-2027 to the end of 2027, exactly when the dated wood and capacity tests fall.

The strongest counter-case. Being the lone stock with positive revisions in a sector the market has not yet started to pay for can attract capital for longer than fundamentals justify, and the broader market regime shows first signs of turning less defensive.

What would change my view. Peers' estimates turning up (a sector move, not a single-stock move); the 200-day moving average rising for several months; or the share of Buy ratings rising again.

Conclusion: sell-side and price momentum are strong now but narrow, leverage-driven and unsupported by peers, with a mechanical fade ahead, so the attribute is met today and is fragile.

Score: 84, set by the Rater. Both measures in the top fifth would give A, but two parts are negative, so B: the share of Buy ratings fell 10 points to 70% as Jefferies and DNB Carnegie moved to Hold, and the 200-day average has risen in only one of the last twelve months, while guidance momentum is limited to the raised savings figure and peers are falling (peers do not pull the letter down on their own). I place it high in B because the revisions are exceptional against the growth rate (consensus EPS +13% over three months, 93rd percentile, and +23% over six, 94th, against about 2.6% revenue growth) and the price is 21% above its 200-day average with target prices up 18%.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The case is simple to state and unusually easy to track, but it is not low-risk: the range of outcomes is wide, the errors lean down, and the share price now carries sentiment risk that it did not carry in the summer.

Simplicity and trackability (the good part)

  • Few drivers, all with public prices. Swedish pulpwood price lists, the kraftliner and testliner indices, EUR/SEK and USD/SEK, and European gas. Few cases can be followed this closely from outside the company.
  • A mechanical conversion from EBITDA to EPS, and guidance given in the same building blocks the forecast is built from.
  • One date settles a lot. On 2 February the liquid packaging board price round, the dividend, the 2027 maintenance plan, capex and management's wording on wood all become known.
  • The balance sheet is not a risk. Even in a bad 2027, leverage peaks near 1.6x to 1.8x EBITDA, against a 2.5x ceiling.

Fragility (the hard part)

  • The range of 2027 outcomes is wide. My distribution for 2027 EBITDA (chart below) puts only 20% to 25% at or above consensus and about one in three below SEK 4.2bn. The first half of 2027 is set to within about ±10%; the second half is open to ±25%.
  • Why the range leans down. Misses have been bigger than beats. Mill curtailments make volume losses worse than proportional. Concentrated buyers cap the upside in board prices. Wages and logistics costs rise by contract, while selling prices must be negotiated.
  • SEK 3.9bn is not a floor. SEK 3.9bn is the part of 2027 EBITDA already secured by actions taken and prices set, and a bad year can go below it. Eleven months before the end of 2026, the most cautious broker's 2026 forecast was still 19% too high.
  • Sudden risks. Six sudden risks are ranked by likelihood in the chart below; the most likely is wood up 10% or more by late 2027 (25% to 30% over 18 months).
  • Sentiment. Billerud is the purest proxy for one story, at the 91st percentile of its five-year forward P/E range, with a dated first test in March 2027. A fair trough valuation is SEK 58 to 67 a share (25% to 35% below today), near 0.55x to 0.6x book value, with a tail to SEK 45 to 50 in a joint shock.

What history says: Billerud's recoveries have been ended by cost, not by demand, and November consensus for the year ahead has tended to be too high.

2011Wood accounted for most of the rise in variable costs; the fourth-quarter margin fell to 4%
2014New containerboard capacity eroded liner prices
2017 to 2018A wood shortage and fibre inflation neutralised price gains
Late 2023 to 2024Beats and a share-price rally, then given back as wood costs rose
2025November consensus for EBITDA was about SEK 5.0bn; the outturn was near SEK 4.1bn

Where I differ from the market. A P/E in the top decile of its five-year range says the market sees Billerud's risk as lower than I do. I think the market is pricing good trackability as if it were a narrow range of outcomes. This case has the first without the second.

The constructive reading: the risks are few, dated and public. Investors can manage them by watching three public series (spring wood price lists, the kraftliner index after March, and the hedge rates newly added each quarter) and by knowing that the next two reports will look good whatever the truth about the second half. Those public series will give the earliest warnings, from about May 2027, months before Billerud's own accounts show them.

What would change my view. Longer board contracts, wood ownership or a closure would narrow the range of outcomes. None is planned.

Conclusion: the case is simple and highly trackable with a safe balance sheet, but the range of outcomes is wide (EPS roughly ±50%), skewed down and now carries re-rating risk, so it is a higher-than-average risk case.

Score: 32, set by the Rater. The case is simple and unusually trackable (few drivers with public monthly prices, a mechanical EBITDA-to-EPS conversion, leverage peaking at about 1.6-1.8x against a 2.5x ceiling), but the memo's 2027 EPS range of SEK 2.2-6.6 around 4.4 is about plus or minus 50%, skewed down, with wood, price and krona correlated in the bad case, sudden risks (wood up 10% or more at 25-30%, a krona surge at about 20%, a board price attack at 15-20%), a history of recoveries ended by cost and consensus too high, and sentiment risk at the 91st percentile of its five-year P/E. Trackability keeps it above Entra's thin-evidence, rate-sensitive case, but the range is wider than Helios Towers', so it sits just below it, between the two Risks groups' 35 and 42 on the downside because the range, not the tracking, sets the risk.

#10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

I read the stock as late in the "turning up" phase but priced as "reinforcing", with two confirming reports ahead and then a fork from mid-2027.

The evidence. Earnings bottomed in the first quarter of 2026, and the second and third quarters beat consensus. Estimates have risen for about six months, and the shares have re-rated from an all-time low on price to book value. The dashboard's rule reads this pattern as Reinforcing.

Why I stop short of the Reinforcing label. Reinforcing implies a thesis that has broadened and is being confirmed from several directions. Billerud's thesis has not broadened. It is still a single mechanism (the price-cost spread), in a single stock (peers' estimates are falling), without support from demand, and two of the five named brokers have already stepped back on valuation. What the thesis does have is two reports ahead that will reinforce it on the surface: the fourth quarter of 2026 up about 40% on a year earlier, and the first quarter of 2027 more than double.

The fork from mid-2027. My rough odds for where the stock stands by late 2027 are about 50% stalling, 25% to 30% broadening or reinforcing, and 15% to 20% collapsing. The chart below shows what each path requires.

Where I differ from the market: the stock is one phase earlier than its price says. The share price and the dashboard rule say Reinforcing. I think the stock is one phase earlier on fundamentals and one phase from stalling on the calendar. I agree that the next five months will look like Reinforcing.

The strongest counter-case. Lifecycle labels follow evidence, and the evidence through April 2027 will be good. If the second half of 2027 then holds, I will have been one phase behind throughout.

What would change my view. A second mechanism (capacity leaving the industry, or volumes growing on end use rather than restocking) and upgrades spreading to peers.

Conclusion: the stock is late in turning up and priced as reinforcing, with a likely move to stalling from mid-2027 unless a supply event broadens the thesis.

Score: 44, set by the Rater. Earnings bottomed in Q1 2026, two quarters beat and estimates have risen for six months, but the thesis has not broadened (one spread mechanism, no demand, peers' estimates falling, two brokers stepping back) and the price already reflects the computed Reinforcing; the next two reports will look strong against a weak base, then the memo puts about 50% on Stalling and 15-20% on Collapsing by late 2027 against 25-30% on broadening. I agree with the memo's 'late in turning up, priced as reinforcing': the good news is largely known with a dated fork ahead, so it sits just below Linea Directa's improvement not yet in forecasts and above National Grid's Stalling.

#11 The fair multiple

The guideline fair multiple is 15.5x two-year-forward earnings, the 90th percentile of the stock's ten-year range, set for the Reinforcing phase. As a P/E, I think 15.5x is at the generous end, but the share value it produces on our earnings is sober. The earnings base matters far more than the multiple.

Three observations.

  1. Two different "current multiples" are in play. On consensus earnings the stock trades on about 13.2x, so the guideline is 17% higher. On the model's lower earnings the same price is 18.0x, so moving to 15.5x is a fall of about 14%. Both statements are true; the difference between them is entirely the gap between consensus and our two-year-forward EPS (about SEK 6.6 against SEK 5.0).
13.2xToday's price on consensus two-year-forward EPS
15.5xGuideline fair multiple, the 90th percentile of ten years
18.0xToday's price on our two-year-forward EPS
  1. The top-decile multiple was earned in different conditions. The stock last traded at 15x to 19x from spring 2020 to the end of 2021, when earnings were about to treble to the 2022 record and large upgrades lay ahead. On my reading of the lifecycle phase (#10) and the scope for upgrades (#7), today's conditions are different. For a stock late in turning up, with forecasts this uncertain, I would centre the fair multiple on the 75th percentile (about 14x) and treat 15.5x as the ceiling.
  2. Yet the share value at 15.5x is not stretched on asset measures. 15.5x applied to our two-year-forward EPS at March 2028 (about SEK 6.0) gives about SEK 93.5 a share. That value is roughly 6x EBITDA and 0.8x book value, about where the stock trades today and close to the 6.5x EBITDA that Jefferies uses. For a business earning 5% to 7% on capital, a price below book value is right. The P/E looks high because operating profit is thin after heavy depreciation, which also makes the P/E a noisy yardstick here: SEK 100m of EBITDA moves the fair value by 5.5%.

Sensitivity: the earnings base outweighs the multiple.

SEK 6Value of each turn of multiple at March 2028, or 7% of today's price
About 4 turnsThe multiple equivalent of a 10% change in forward EBITDA
Where I differ from the market: my quarrel is with the earnings, not the multiple. The market pays about 13x to 13.5x on consensus earnings, slightly above the ten-year median. I have no quarrel with that multiple; my quarrel is with the earnings it is applied to.

The strongest counter-case. High P/Es on below-normal earnings are normal for cyclicals, and our 2028 EPS is still below mid-cycle. On mid-cycle EPS of SEK 6.0 to 6.5, today's price is about 14x to 15x, which is unremarkable.

What would change my view. A closure or a proven second leg of upgrades would justify a top-decile multiple. Evidence of stalling would pull the fair multiple to the median (12.7x) or below.

Conclusion: the guideline 15.5x is a fair ceiling rather than a centre for a stock at this stage, and it yields a share value near today's price on our earnings, so valuation offers no cushion.

Score: 32, set by the Rater. Dear on the own-range measure and neutral against peers gives D. I place it in the lower part of the band because the dearness is not flattering: the 87th percentile is on consensus earnings the memo thinks 22% too high (on the model's EPS the price is 18x against a 15.5x guideline already at the 90th percentile), and a stock late in turning up with a likely stall ahead deserves nearer the 75th percentile or the median, not the top decile; only the 0.8x book and the cyclical's below-mid-cycle earnings keep it off the floor.

#13 Summary conclusion

Billerud is a medium-quality cyclical in the first year of a genuine spread recovery, run by a disciplined management, with the strongest balance sheet among its direct peers. The recovery is not in doubt. What is in doubt is a second step of earnings growth that consensus and the share price already assume.

What I am most confident of

  • 2027 EBITDA will be well above 2026 (about 95% likely), and the next two reports will look strong.
  • The controllable SEK 0.45bn of 2027 EBITDA improvement will be delivered.
  • The balance sheet will not be a problem, and Gävle will absorb the cash that might otherwise have funded buybacks.

What decides the case

  • Whether wood costs stay low after the salvage supply ends, whether price holds once UK recycled capacity runs, and where the krona goes. A plausible error in each is worth SEK 0.8 to 1.4 of EPS, and in the bad case the three move together.
  • Whether capacity leaves European board. A closure is the only route to a second leg of improvement and the only unpriced positive of size, and it has no date.

What makes the case worth following

  • The evidence arrives on known dates and in public prices. The favourable window runs to about April 2027 and the real test runs from July to October 2027, so an investor can know in advance which evidence matters and which does not.
  • Billerud would become unusually skewed to the positive on a closure announcement, on proof that price holds as wood costs rise, or at a share price nearer book-value support.

The four memo ratings

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 58, set by the Rater. The input forces are clearly positive but modest and front-loaded (Tailwinds 54, Internal change 58), and they reach profits with high certainty in 2027 (EBITDA up about a third, about 95% likely well above 2026), but that output is a recovery from a trough to only average margins by 2030, largely in the run-rate already and facing dated counter-forces from mid-2027 (Forecast financials C, 64). A real but mild net positive that restores rather than raises earnings power sits in the high 50s, below the clearly positive cases in the low 60s.

Foundations' Robustness: 37, set by the Rater. Quality of the business at 35 sets it: real niche moats, a tariff-protected North American unit and the strongest balance sheet among non-integrated peers sit on a business with no forest, little pricing power outside scarce grades, the marginal-cost position in its European grades and returns below the cost of capital. The delivery record (Guidance and delivery 40: dependable quarterly blocks, but large misses, a cut margin target and a cut dividend) does nothing to lift it, so it sits above the levels' price-taker examples (Maersk 30) only on its balance sheet and niches.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 55, set by the Rater. In substance the case fits the memo's 'CfC in quality cyclical at trough-on-trough, leading to reversion to normal' (CfC: cause for concern) in kind: the cause for concern (the 2022-25 wood shock) is clearing and the forecast is precisely a reversion to average margins. But one important element is missing, quality (Foundations 37, below CVS Group's middling quality that Richard put at 65-75 for a clearing CfC), and current problems blur it (North American execution, a cut dividend, a defensive capital call); the memo's point that the trough was six months and 43% ago is timing and price, judged in topics 7 and 12, so I do not count it and place it above the memo's D.

Case Riskiness: 31, set by the Rater. Riskiness and simplicity at 32 sets it: a simple, trackable case with public drivers and no balance-sheet risk does not offset an EPS range of about plus or minus 50% skewed down, correlated wood, price and krona drivers in the bad case, and a share price at a top-decile multiple carried by one company-specific upgrade story. That is close to the levels' wide-range single-mechanism cases at about 25, lifted a little above them by the safe balance sheet and the dated, public tests.

End notes

Bases. EBITDA and EPS are on the brokers' adjusted basis (before items affecting comparability). Forecasts are the Financial Analyst's model (model update 1); I have changed no forecast input. The latest Earnings Review covers the quarter to 30 September 2026, reported on 22 October 2026, so the earlier caution about its date is resolved.

Forecast table (#6). FY2026 EPS is SEK 1.09 at a normal 22% tax rate; the model's SEK 1.19 uses the lower tax rate actually booked in the three reported quarters. The model's single-quarter figure for Q4 2026 is a balancing number between two EBITDA bases and should not be quoted; the expectation for Q4 2026 EBITDA is about SEK 1.16bn. The model's notes still describe a currency hedge "roll-off" in mid-2027; later research shows the hedges are a rolling programme, which changes the wording and not the numbers.

For the Financial Analyst (#12). Please check the timing of dividends in the model: each fiscal year's dividend appears to reduce net debt in that same year, when it is declared for the year and paid the following spring. The corrected 18-month return of about +6.6% in #12 reflects payment of the FY2027 dividend in about May 2028.

Share-price change over six months (#0, #8). The memo gives Billerud's six-month rise as 43% (dashboard technical measures) and as 39% (the peer comparison); the two figures may rest on different measurement dates, and I have kept both as stated.

Charts. Charts drawn for this page (run-rate, sensitivity, EBITDA bridge, quarterly path, outcome distribution, return range, the three routes to 2027 EBITDA and the upgrade-phase timeline) and the diagrams written into the page take their figures from the memo. The 2026 quarterly EBITDA figures on the adjusted basis are implied by the memo's growth rates. Default charts and tables come from FactSet and the Financial Analyst's model (update 1); their notes give the basis of each.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
